COLUMN-NAMING DIFFERENCE FROM THE 2022 BOOK: here the gross payout column is 'Gross Value' and the columns under the 'Realized Return' merged header ('Net Return', '% Return', 'Multiple') are NET OF COST (Net Return == Net Value, e.g. Alabama -$1,980.44 = 499.56 - 2,480). In the 2022 book the column literally called 'Realized Return' is the GROSS payout. I populated expected.realized_return and expected_owners.realized with the GROSS figure in both files so the tie-out engine compares like with like. The workbook's own net figures are recoverable as gross - cost.

TRADE: the workbook has a 'Secondary Trades' block with exactly one line - 'Sam sells 25% of Alabama to Ed (3/14)'. Its cash consideration is not stated; I derived -$620.00 (25% x $2,480 lot price) because the Players table carries the trade at cost: Sam's Entry is $10,653 vs $11,273 in the Bid Summary (-$620) and Ed's is $3,515 vs $2,895 (+$620). So the trade settled at exactly pro-rata lot cost. Both the cost split and the 0.75/0.25 payout split are confirmed by the workbook's own owner-level totals - no discrepancy.

Because the trade is carried at cost, expected_owners[].cost is POST-TRADE (Players table) while the Bid Summary 'Total Paid' is PRE-TRADE. Both are in this file: Bid Summary pre-trade totals are Chris H. $2,050, Craig T. $930, Ed Z. $2,895, Henry A. $470, Matt M. $3,075, Sam R. $11,273, Zach L. $8,791, Zack M. $3,820 (sum $33,304).
